The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- A single prominent white/tan circular spot (center of leaf)
- Scattered dark green water-soaked spots in the upper area
- Otherwise healthy green leaf

This is a **leaf** disease. Top candidates from the KB: Holcus_Spot, Eyespot, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Tar_Spot. Let me check references one at a time.
Holcus Spot reference shows a single tan/white circular spot on a green leaf, very similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates.
Eyespot shows numerous small spots with concentric ring patterns all over the leaf - very different from the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Physoderma Brown Spot shows many small spots in bands with dark midrib lesions - very different. Let me check Tar Spot.
Tar Spot shows black raised glossy spots scattered across the leaf - different from test image. Let me check a few more candidates.
Common Rust shows orange/reddish elongated pustules - not matching. Let me check Southern Rust and Carbonum Leaf Spot.
Southern Rust shows dense orange pustules - not matching. Let me check Carbonum Leaf Spot.
Carbonum Leaf Spot shows many tan/brown spots with darker borders arranged along veins - different from test image. Let me view a second Holcus Spot reference to confirm the match.

This second Holcus Spot reference confirms the match strongly. It shows scattered white/tan circular spots on a green leaf, with the same appearance as the test image: round, papery white/tan spots with some water-soaked areas nearby.

The test image matches Holcus Spot very well:
- White/tan circular spot with papery texture
- Dark green water-soaked spots nearby (early-stage lesions)
- Spots randomly distributed on the leaf
- Spot size consistent (~1/4 inch)
- On an otherwise green, healthy leaf
